subtitle: Build on the contributions people have actually demonstrated, combine those strengths thoughtfully across the team and make room for growth with the right support.
scope: For staff, team coordinators and leaders across DSD and DHS. Original practice cases develop practical ways to recognize and combine contributions; the course is not a strengths assessment, selection instrument or authorization to change a position or employment decision. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Actual assignment, equity-analysis and reporting responsibilities remain. No personal cultural or IDI profile is created. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters go to the person or area responsible within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: A useful strength is a contribution you can explain in its setting, not a permanent label that settles what someone can or should do. Examine a practice resource team, understand particular meanings of showing ability, combine different contributions and compare a supported learning opportunity with repeating the familiar assignment. You can recognize dependable work and still make room for development. A comfortable private reflection can help you understand your own meanings without becoming a public biography or a personnel score.

lessons.title: Describe a demonstrated contribution
lessons.summary: Recognize a strength through a particular example rather than a general personality label.
lessons.objective: Describe a useful contribution and the conditions in which it helped.
objectives: Describe a useful contribution and the conditions in which it helped.
Distinguish demonstrated skill, interest and an unsupported permanent type.
Choose a work inquiry that adds relevant evidence to the practice team’s description.
takeaways: A specific contribution is more informative than a broad label.
Support and context help explain the result.
Evidence of one skill does not establish every future role.
lessons.statement: Name what the person contributed, how it helped and what made it possible.

intro.heading: A useful description keeps the work visible
intro.body:
In a practice DSD resource team, Xan prepares a comparison table that makes differences between two approved examples easier to locate. Kei asks follow-up questions that help the group notice an unclear instruction. Dia gives a concise explanation of the agreed revision. All three contributions help the same work. Coordinator Morgan calls Xan the detail person, Kei the people person and Dia the natural leader. Those labels conceal more than they explain.

A more useful description identifies an action and its effect. Xan organized the supplied information so the comparison could be checked. Kei asked which instruction a first reader would use, exposing a question the draft had left open. Dia explained the actual revision and its limit, keeping the presentation accurate. These statements let the team discuss the contributions without pretending that three work examples reveal a permanent personality.

The context also matters. Xan had current examples and time to check the columns. Kei could examine the draft before the conversation. Dia used an explanation the responsible role had confirmed. A contribution supported by those conditions does not prove that the person needs no preparation on a future unfamiliar task. Nor does lack of an example show that another colleague cannot learn the skill.

The Canada School of Public Service’s team-charter guidance invites teams to identify skills and knowledge members bring and areas they want to develop. It is a bounded planning reference here, not a Minnesota assignment rule or a required assessment. The practice exercise uses an ordinary contribution description: the task, what the person did, the result and the useful conditions. No proprietary strengths categories or score are needed.

For practice, replace one of Morgan’s labels with a precise description. Keep the distinction between what is demonstrated and what remains unknown. You can value a contribution without claiming that the person should perform it forever, has no other interests or is qualified for every role that resembles it.

lessons.keyStatement: A demonstrated contribution supports a specific statement, not an unlimited claim about the person.

flashcards.back: An action in a particular setting that helped the work; its effect and relevant conditions can be described.
An ability applied to a task. A useful example can show it in a setting without establishing a permanent personality.
Something a person would like to explore or develop; ask rather than infer it from earlier assignments.
A different contribution that connects with another to support the same work.
A defined chance to practice with suitable support and review within actual responsibilities.
The task, resources, preparation, people and conditions that help explain a contribution.

items.title: Name the action
items.body: Xan organized supplied information in a checkable table. That description can be examined and learned from. Calling Xan naturally precise does not show which comparison mattered, whether the source was current or how another person might learn to do it.

items.title: Name the effect
items.body: Kei’s question made an unclear instruction visible. That is more specific than being good with people. The useful effect concerns the draft, not a claim that Kei must handle every relationship or can decide all policy questions.

items.title: Name the support
items.body: Dia had a confirmed explanation and preparation. Those conditions are part of the result. Recognizing them does not take credit away from Dia; it makes the contribution understandable and keeps a later unfamiliar presentation from being treated as automatic.

tabs.label: A permanent type
tabs.body: A label such as natural leader can make a person’s present role seem inevitable. It may hide preparation and other interests. In this case, Dia’s clear explanation is evidence of that contribution; it does not decide appointment, promotion or every future team role.

tabs.label: Only the final result
tabs.body: Saying the presentation went well recognizes something useful but leaves out which action helped. It also gives little guidance for learning or combining contributions. Describe the accurate explanation and its conditions so the result is more than general praise.

tabs.label: An example with conditions
tabs.body: The table, reader question and explanation each support a precise description. The team can ask what preparation helped and what remains unknown. This keeps recognition and learning connected without treating the three colleagues as fixed categories.

check.question: Which description best fits Xan’s supplied contribution?
check.correct: Xan made the supplied examples easier to compare through a checked table, using current material and preparation time.
wrong: Xan is permanently the detail person and cannot benefit from another role.
The table proves Xan can independently approve any policy revision.
Colleagues without a table example have no ability to develop that skill.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The description connects the particular action, useful effect and conditions without exceeding the evidence.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A permanent type adds a limit on Xan that the example does not establish. A checked comparison does not grant policy approval authority. Missing an example does not prove someone cannot learn. Each alternative turns limited evidence into a claim about role, authority or potential.

items.text: Xan organized the supplied differences into a checkable table.
Dia explained the confirmed revision accurately.
Would Xan like to practice explaining the comparison?
Would Kei like to learn how to prepare the table?
Dia can approve any policy because the explanation was clear.
Xan must always be assigned the same task.

lessons.title: Understand how showing ability can carry different meanings
lessons.summary: Connect two particular learned meanings to an invitation that recognizes contribution without pressure.
lessons.objective: Explain Rosa’s and Vale’s meanings the people describe of showing ability.
objectives: Explain Rosa’s and Vale’s meanings the people describe of showing ability.

Choose an invitation that keeps actual choice and a useful contribution visible.
takeaways: A visible attempt can invite shared learning.
Ask about the meaning before making a personal type.
lessons.statement: A contribution can be visible in different ways without making one person more worthy.

intro.heading: Showing what you can do is also a meaning question
intro.body:
In an original practice neighborhood repair circle, Rosa checks that the shared tools are ready before visitors arrive. Rosa learned in a familiar family gathering that preparing quietly spared a guest the burden of asking and kept attention on the shared purpose. Naming the preparation in a short factual acknowledgment is welcome; giving a speech about Rosa’s character is not. Rosa explains this particular meaning rather than claiming that everyone in a community behaves the same way.

Vale learned in a small rehearsal group that trying a short demonstration aloud gave others something concrete to respond to. The visible attempt was an invitation to learn together, not a claim to be better than everyone. Vale volunteers to show a simple way of arranging the repair table and expects people to suggest changes. Rosa initially reads the demonstration as wanting praise. Vale initially reads Rosa’s quiet preparation as lack of interest in contributing.

The two explanations widen those first frames. Rosa can recognize that Vale’s attempt invites a shared improvement. Vale can recognize that Rosa already contributed care through preparation. They do not have to adopt every practice of the other person. They can arrange a brief demonstration, acknowledge the prepared tools accurately and ask whether Rosa wants any additional part. Neither contribution requires a public personal story.

The Council of Europe’s intercultural guidance describes personalized, contextual meanings and the value of understanding another perspective while reflecting on one’s own. That helps shape the conversation in this example. It does not establish a quiet-helper type or an outspoken-demonstrator type. Rosa and Vale have supplied particular learned meanings; the next person’s meaning remains unknown until there is a reason and a suitable way to understand it.

In the DHS fiction, Morgan cannot borrow Rosa’s account to explain Xan or Vale’s account to explain Dia. Instead, Morgan can ask a relevant work question: what helped the contribution, how would the person like it accurately recognized and which skill would they like to develop? A contribution discussion can become more open when it does not make public confidence the sole proof of ability or quietness a reason for permanent support work.

inThisLesson: Read the meanings the people describe.
lessons.keyStatement: Understand the person’s account rather than infer ability or motive from visibility alone.

accordion.heading: Follow meaning into a revised response

items.title: Rosa’s preparation
items.body: The tools were ready and Rosa describes care through reducing a guest’s burden. This explains a contribution that preceded the public activity. A brief accurate acknowledgment can recognize it without turning a chosen quiet role into permanent invisibility or demanding a character speech.

items.title: Vale’s demonstration
items.body: Vale describes a visible attempt as an opening for shared learning. That explanation revises Rosa’s initial praise-seeking interpretation. The group can respond to the actual arrangement rather than assume a confident performance establishes superiority or removes the need for feedback.

items.title: A wider invitation
items.body: An invitation can retain the demonstration, recognize the preparation and offer a particular optional next part. It does not need everyone to perform the same social style. The new response comes from the meanings the people describe and actual task, not a country label or a test of belonging.

tabs.label: Require the same public performance
tabs.body: Making Rosa demonstrate as proof of contribution would ignore the work already done and the stated preference about public attention. The activity needs ready tools and an understandable arrangement, not identical performances from everyone. Invite a useful part rather than impose a personal display.

tabs.label: Keep the helper permanently hidden
tabs.body: Avoiding all factual acknowledgment because Rosa values quiet preparation would confuse a preference about spectacle with a wish to erase work. The supplied account welcomes a brief statement. Ask accurately and avoid making the previous support contribution a permanent assignment.

tabs.label: Recognize and offer a choice
tabs.body: Name the prepared tools, let Vale demonstrate the arrangement and ask Rosa about a specific additional part. This respects both meanings while keeping actual participation open. It supports a usable table without assuming every preference or every future contribution is settled.

check.question: What changes after Rosa and Vale explain their meanings?
check.correct: Their first interpretations become more specific: preparation can express care and a visible attempt can invite shared learning.
wrong: The accounts establish every quiet person’s cultural type.
Rosa must accept a public personal speech for the contribution to count.
Vale’s demonstration proves superior worth and no need for feedback.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The accounts revise the first frames without turning either person into a permanent category.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Two supplied accounts cannot establish a quiet-person type. Rosa’s work does not need a personal speech to matter. Vale’s visible attempt invites response rather than proving greater worth. Each alternative converts a useful meaning into a type, performance gate or ranking.

items.text: Rosa describes preparation as sparing visitors the burden of asking.
Vale describes a visible attempt as inviting shared learning.
Briefly acknowledge the prepared tools accurately.
Invite a specific next part without demanding a personal speech.
Every quiet person wants permanent support work.
A demonstration proves greater personal worth.

move.failure: Visibility becomes a culture label or a required performance of worth.

lessons.title: Build a contribution inventory that can change
lessons.summary: Keep demonstrated skills, desired practice and needed support distinct in a useful team discussion.
lessons.objective: Separate demonstrated contribution, stated interest and needed preparation in the practice inventory.
objectives: Separate demonstrated contribution, stated interest and needed preparation in the practice inventory.
Identify why an inventory should not become a permanent personal ranking.
Choose a next inquiry that makes a proposed learning opportunity concrete.
takeaways: Ask what people would like to develop.
Keep interest distinct from present readiness.
An inventory is a working description, not a fixed identity.
lessons.statement: Describe what is shown now and what the person wants to practice next.

image.caption: People at a training table listen as one participant makes a point.

intro.heading: A strength description should open a conversation
intro.body:
Morgan revises the practice team’s list into three questions: what contribution is demonstrated here, what would the person like to develop and what support would make the next part feasible? Xan says the comparison table is familiar and would like practice explaining it. Kei says asking reader questions is useful and would like to learn how the checked columns are prepared. Dia would like to understand the source comparison behind the explanation, not only repeat the final presentation.

These statements are related but different. Xan’s table is an example of current skill. The interest in explaining it is an actual statement, not proof of readiness for an unfamiliar presentation. Needed preparation is another question. Keeping the three parts visible helps Morgan consider a particular opportunity instead of treating interest as an automatic appointment or current skill as a limit on growth.

A modest inventory can record the task-related contribution and the stated interest for the actual planning purpose. It does not need a cultural type, a private family history or an unofficial colleague ranking. Relevant work information should be handled through appropriate agency practices. The course exercise uses fiction; a learning note is not a new employment record or a grant of access to someone else’s personnel information.

Notice the question the inventory can reveal. Kei has had few chances to prepare the table because the familiar arrangement assigns that part to Xan. Lack of a table example may reflect lack of opportunity, not lack of potential. The team can examine a defined practice task, a checked example and support. That does not mean every colleague receives an identical rotation regardless of qualifications, current duties or the real decision role.

The Surgeon General’s 2022 workplace framework discusses growth, training and relevant reciprocal feedback. This course uses those planning ideas as guidance, not a Minnesota employment mandate, a promise of promotion or a health prediction. A useful inventory invites a clear next conversation: what could be practiced, which preparation is needed and who has responsibility for the assignment?

lessons.keyStatement: A working inventory distinguishes evidence, interest and support rather than combining them into a personal score.

items.title: Demonstrated does not mean permanent
items.body: Xan’s table is useful evidence of a contribution in this setting. Keeping Xan on every table forever would add an assignment rule the example does not establish. The same evidence can help plan an explanation opportunity with appropriate preparation.

items.title: Interested does not mean ready for everything
items.body: Kei wants to learn the checked columns. That supplies an interest and a reason to discuss practice, not proof of readiness for every technical or policy task. A defined example, time and feedback can make the learning proposal explainable.

items.title: Missing does not mean incapable
items.body: Dia has not supplied a source-checking example in the current arrangement. A missing example is unknown. Ask about relevant experience and possible preparation rather than confuse a previous division of work with a permanent limit on ability.

tabs.heading: Compare ways to use the inventory

tabs.label: A rank of people
tabs.body: Turning the inventory into a best-to-worst list collapses different tasks and conditions. Xan’s table, Kei’s question and Dia’s explanation help in different ways. A ranking would not answer what the next task needs and could hide interests the people actually stated.

tabs.label: An automatic new role
tabs.body: Assigning Kei full source authority merely because of the learning interest confuses willingness with readiness and authorized responsibility. A useful practice part can be narrower. Keep the actual decision role and needed preparation in the proposed arrangement.

tabs.label: A task-related planning aid
tabs.body: Record the example, chosen interest and support question for the current planning purpose. The team can examine a feasible next part and revisit the description when evidence changes. This gives strengths a practical use without a permanent personnel type.

check.question: How should Morgan read Kei’s interest in preparing checked columns?
check.correct: As a stated learning interest that needs a defined practice part, suitable preparation and the actual assignment role.
wrong: As proof Kei can approve every source or policy condition.
As proof the existing reader-question contribution has no value.
As an automatic guarantee of appointment or promotion.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The interest can inform a useful opportunity while readiness, support and actual authority remain visible.
check.feedbackIncorrect: An interest grants no source or policy approval authority. Wanting to learn another part does not erase Kei’s useful question contribution. A practice proposal guarantees no appointment or promotion. The three shortcuts confuse learning with authority, replacement or an employment outcome.

items.text: Xan prepared the checkable comparison table.
Kei exposed an unclear reader instruction.
Xan wants practice explaining the table.
Dia wants to understand the source comparison.
What checked example could support Kei’s practice?
What time and guidance would the proposed part require?

options: Dia is incapable of learning the table because an example is missing.
The interest automatically authorizes Dia to decide all sources.
Dia’s interest can inform a defined practice proposal while actual experience and preparation remain to be examined.
responses: A missing example is not evidence of incapacity.
A stated interest does not create decision authority.
This preserves the actual contribution and interest while keeping the next conditions honest.

lessons.transfer: Privately separate one demonstrated contribution, one stated interest and one support question from the example.

move.control: You can use a contribution inventory as an evolving planning conversation.
move.failure: A planning description becomes a rank, guaranteed outcome or permanent limit on growth.

lessons.title: Combine strengths through a clear connection
lessons.summary: Explain how different contributions help the same work without creating fixed team types.
lessons.objective: Describe how the practice table, reader question and explanation connect.
objectives: Describe how the practice table, reader question and explanation connect.
Identify a dependency that complementary contributions do not remove.
Choose a task arrangement that makes responsibility and useful support clear.
takeaways: Different skills can help the same purpose.
Connections matter as well as individual contribution.
Combining strengths does not remove a needed condition.
lessons.statement: Make the connection explainable instead of simply assembling different labels.

image.caption: People at a training table listen as one participant makes a point.

intro.heading: Complementarity needs an actual task
intro.body:
The resource team will compare a revised learning example with its current approved explanation. Xan’s table can show the supplied differences. Kei’s reader question can reveal whether the sequence is understandable. Dia’s concise explanation can communicate the change and its limit. These are complementary contributions because their effects connect to the same purpose, not because the people belong to three permanent types.

Morgan makes the connection concrete. The comparison table must identify which information is current. The reader inquiry must concern the actual example rather than an unrelated service question. The explanation must distinguish an approved statement from an issue still needing a responsible source role. A polished presentation cannot compensate for a missing source condition, and a careful table cannot by itself establish how a first reader experiences the draft.

The team can agree on a useful handoff: a checked comparison, the specific reader question and the confirmed explanation. The responsible roles retain actual authority. A coordinator can help clarify these contributions within the work arrangement; the learning exercise does not assign official approval or let a team vote away a needed policy condition. The program’s consultant can guide the equity inquiry and offer feedback without taking over staff’s work.

Complementarity also permits learning. Xan can practice a defined part of the explanation, with Dia offering useful preparation feedback, while Kei examines a checked table example. That arrangement is a proposal to examine through actual assignment roles, not an automatic requirement that everyone perform every task. Combining present contributions and creating practice opportunities answer different questions, and both deserve attention.

For practice, explain why the three contributions connect, which condition they still need and how one supported learning part could fit. Use the example. There is no need to create a new personality grid. A clear account of the task, contribution and connection gives the team more useful direction than a claim that every type is represented.

lessons.keyStatement: Complementary contributions help when the connection and needed conditions are clear.

items.title: The table supports an inquiry
items.body: Xan’s checked columns make a particular difference visible so Kei can ask about its meaning for the reader. An unchecked or outdated table would weaken that connection. Complementarity includes the useful condition, not merely appreciation of two different skills.

items.title: The question supports an explanation
items.body: Kei’s inquiry reveals the unclear sequence that Dia’s explanation needs to address. It does not authorize an answer to every service question. A useful connection keeps the exact reader issue and confirmed content together rather than allowing a confident response to outrun the source.

items.title: The explanation supports shared understanding
items.body: Dia can state the confirmed revision and its limit. That helps colleagues use the comparison appropriately. It does not erase another contribution or settle a source condition still open; presentation quality and actual authority are separate.

tabs.label: Different labels without a connection
tabs.body: Having a detail person, people person and leader type says little about the actual work. It can make the arrangement sound complete before sources, sequence and responsibilities are understood. Explain what each contribution does and where the parts depend on one another.

tabs.label: One polished output replaces every check
tabs.body: Treating Dia’s clear explanation as proof of the entire revision would hide the source and reader questions. A visible result can be valuable without answering all conditions. The table and inquiry need their own appropriate checks before the explanation claims a confirmed change.

tabs.label: Connected task and responsibility
tabs.body: A checked table informs the particular reader inquiry, and a confirmed explanation responds to that issue. Each contribution keeps a purpose and a limit. The team can consider a supported practice part without turning a connection into unlimited authority or a compulsory role rotation.

check.question: Why are the three contributions complementary in this example?
check.correct: They support connected parts of the same comparison, reader inquiry and accurate explanation while retaining the source condition and responsible roles.
wrong: Their permanent personality types guarantee success on every task.
A concise explanation removes the need for a current source.
The team can vote to grant each person any policy authority needed.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The task connection explains the value of the contributions and keeps remaining conditions visible.
check.feedbackIncorrect: No permanent types or universal success are established. A clear explanation cannot make an outdated or unresolved source current. A team vote cannot create policy authority. Each alternative replaces an actual task connection with a guarantee, missing condition or invented decision role.

sorting.heading: Separate contribution, connection and open condition

items.text: Xan makes the supplied differences visible in a table.
Dia gives a concise explanation of the confirmed change.
The table helps Kei identify the exact reader question.
The confirmed explanation addresses the actual sequence issue.
The relevant source condition still needs its appropriate role.
Practice preparation and current responsibilities need confirmation.

options: Keep the useful explanation and obtain the needed source condition through the actual responsible role.
Treat presentation quality as approval of every source.
Assign permanent types so no further connection needs examining.
responses: This preserves the demonstrated contribution without hiding a condition it cannot answer.
Clarity cannot grant approval or establish a current source.
Types would not resolve the task dependency or actual responsibility.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain one contribution connection and the condition it does not remove.

move.control: You can describe complementarity through the actual task and its dependencies.
move.failure: A pleasing mix of labels conceals an unresolved source or decision condition.

lessons.title: Use strengths to support growth instead of fixing roles
lessons.summary: Compare a familiar assignment with a defined practice opportunity and relevant feedback.
lessons.objective: Compare the consequences of repeating a familiar task and supporting a new practice part.
objectives: Compare the consequences of repeating a familiar task and supporting a new practice part.
Identify preparation, choice and actual authority needed for the practice proposal.
Preserve the immediate manager duty in the separate protected-class allegation.
takeaways: Current skill can support learning rather than restrict it.
A practice opportunity needs a defined part and feedback.
Actual reporting responsibilities do not wait for learning.
lessons.statement: Let demonstrated skill inform a next opportunity without deciding the person’s future.

image.caption: People at a training table listen as one participant makes a point.

intro.heading: Being good at a task need not mean doing only that task
intro.body:
Morgan considers two practice arrangements. The first keeps Xan on all tables, Kei on all reader conversations and Dia on every explanation because those parts are familiar. The second proposes a defined explanation part for Xan, a checked-column practice part for Kei and a source-comparison learning part for Dia. Both need an actual work decision. The second gives the stated interests a place in the proposal instead of allowing yesterday’s distribution to become each person’s future.

A practice part should be precise enough to prepare and review. Xan could explain one confirmed difference, then hear whether the explanation kept the source and reader question clear. Kei could use one checked example to practice the columns with feedback on the actual comparison. Dia could examine why one source condition needs a responsible role. None of these tasks requires pretending that the person is already qualified for every related responsibility.

Growth also needs feasible conditions. What current work remains? Which resource or example is suitable? Who can provide relevant feedback, and who decides the assignment? A positive invitation is incomplete until these conditions are examined. It should not simply add every new part to existing work or make a staff member repay a learning opportunity through unlimited help. In actual work, apply the real assignment and selection rules.

Actual equity responsibilities remain part of the work. DHS requires an equity lens in daily action and formal analysis for qualifying actions with prolonged or long-term impacts scheduled for the specified leadership approval. This practice exercise can help staff ask better questions, but it does not replace that analysis or the relevant decision role. The consultant leads program guidance and feedback while staff develop and carry their own work.

In a separate practice exchange, manager Marin receives an allegation that a colleague is excluded from explanation opportunities because of national-origin stereotypes. Under MMB Policy 1436, managers and supervisors must immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. Calling the exclusion a strengths preference cannot dismiss or delay that duty. Nonretaliation applies; the course makes no finding. Compare the learning proposal on its own evidence and keep this separate actual responsibility immediate.

inThisLesson: Compare the familiar and new part.
lessons.keyStatement: A supported opportunity responds to a stated interest without inventing readiness, approval or an employment outcome.

items.title: Use current skill as a resource
items.body: Xan’s table knowledge can support an accurate explanation of one difference. The current skill is an asset for learning, not proof that Xan must never explain. The practice can build from what is known without promising mastery of every presentation.

items.title: Give feedback on the actual task
items.body: A response to Kei’s column practice should explain what makes the comparison checkable and which condition remains. Calling Kei talented or unsuitable gives little direction. Relevant feedback can recognize progress while retaining a specific next question.

items.title: Keep the actual duty separate
items.body: Marin receives a protected-class allegation, not merely an inventory preference. The immediate reporting and agency procedures remain. A growth discussion neither substantiates the allegation nor provides permission to hold it until the team agrees on roles.

tabs.label: Repeat the familiar indefinitely
tabs.body: The familiar arrangement may be practical for a particular task, but repeating it without examining interests can hide development opportunities. Current competence does not establish permanent preference. Ask about a defined next part rather than assume that recognition and unchanged assignment are the same thing.

tabs.label: Offer everything without support
tabs.body: Giving all three colleagues every new responsibility sounds generous but leaves preparation and current work unexplained. It may create confusion rather than learning. A smaller supported part can have a clearer purpose and feedback while actual roles decide feasibility.

tabs.label: Define practice and feedback
tabs.body: A confirmed explanation part, checked example and relevant source-comparison inquiry respond to the actual interests. Support and responsible roles still need confirmation. The proposal creates something meaningful to examine without a guarantee of appointment, promotion or instant competence.

check.question: What makes the proposed practice opportunity useful?
check.correct: A stated interest, a defined part, suitable preparation, relevant feedback and an actual assignment decision.
wrong: A permanent strengths type assigns the person’s future automatically.
A positive invitation removes all need to check current responsibilities.
Marin can delay the protected-class allegation until the team chooses roles.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The proposal can be examined and supported without treating enthusiasm or a label as authority.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A permanent type is not an actual assignment decision. A positive invitation does not create unlimited capacity or preparation. Marin’s immediate manager reporting duty cannot wait for the team’s role discussion. The alternatives confuse a label, a promise or learning with the conditions that apply.

items.text: Xan explains one confirmed difference.
Kei prepares columns using a checked example.
Suitable preparation time within current responsibilities.
Relevant task feedback through an appropriate role.
Marin immediately reports the protected-class allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer.
Use required formal equity analysis where the actual DHS policy applies.

lessons.title: Review the contribution and the next opportunity
lessons.summary: Recognize specific learning without a permanent score or a claim about everyone’s experience.
lessons.objective: Describe the supplied practice result at its actual scope.
objectives: Describe the supplied practice result at its actual scope.
Distinguish a new task and missing account from the completed example.
Explain a legitimate private insight without a work-output requirement.
takeaways: A useful practice result has a particular scope.
New work can reveal a new preparation question.
Private understanding need not become a personnel measure.
lessons.statement: Let the actual result inform the next question instead of turning it into a fixed identity.

intro.heading: The description can change as the evidence changes
intro.body:
The final resource-team fiction supplies a small trial after appropriate roles confirm the practice parts and support. Xan explains one checked difference accurately, Kei prepares a usable comparison with the example and Dia identifies why the remaining source question needs the responsible role. These are new demonstrated contributions. They do not replace all earlier skills or prove universal readiness for every related task.

Xan says the defined explanation helped connect table preparation to the reader question. Kei says the checked example made the column purpose understandable. Dia says examining the source condition clarified what the explanation should not promise. Each account describes a particular learning experience. Another colleague’s account is not supplied. The trial does not establish that everyone preferred the arrangement or that every opportunity in the division is equitable.

The next request involves an unfamiliar example and a different source condition. The team can update its description: what the person has demonstrated, which interest remains and what preparation the next part needs. The earlier result is useful evidence, not a guarantee that context never changes. A new question does not erase the real progress, and the real progress does not answer every new question.

Rosa’s and Vale’s encounter may also support a meaningful private insight. You may recognize why you once read visible demonstration as a claim of superiority or quiet preparation as disinterest. Understanding the meanings the people describe can widen that first frame. You do not have to publish a memory, adopt another person’s style or prove an improved workplace measure for that learning to matter.

For final practice, state one demonstrated new contribution, one next condition and one meaning you now understand more fully. Keep the reflection private if you prefer and use the example. A strengths-based discussion is useful when it helps people recognize and connect real contributions while leaving choice, development and actual responsibilities open. It does not need an unofficial score or a permanent best role for every person.

lessons.keyStatement: Specific evidence can expand a contribution description without turning it into a permanent rank.

accordion.heading: Use the result without overstating it

items.title: Recognize the new example
items.body: Xan, Kei and Dia demonstrate particular contributions in the supported trial. Those examples can broaden the working description. They do not show that every possible task is familiar or that a learning exercise determines appointment, promotion or official source authority.

items.title: Examine the changed task
items.body: The unfamiliar example has its own source and preparation needs. The prior trial helps identify questions; it does not remove them. Treat the new condition as part of the actual work rather than proof the earlier learning was worthless or that further support is unnecessary.

items.title: Keep the personal insight legitimate
items.body: Rosa’s and Vale’s meanings can change an initial interpretation without requiring a public memory or work metric. Private self-understanding is a valid outcome. It remains distinct from colleagues’ actual task evidence and does not justify assigning them a cultural type.

tabs.label: Permanent mastery
tabs.body: Declaring everyone a master of every part would exceed the small trial and could hide support needed for unfamiliar work. The actual new contributions are valuable without a universal guarantee. Name their conditions so the next arrangement can be considered responsibly.

tabs.label: No value until a perfect measure
tabs.body: Rejecting the trial because it lacks a division-wide strengths score would ignore the usable comparison, accurate explanation and supplied accounts. A modest supported result can matter. It does not need a made-up personal assessment or a claim that all opportunity gaps are solved.

tabs.label: Specific progress and next question
tabs.body: Describe the new examples and the three particular accounts, then retain the unfamiliar task and unsupplied experience. This makes the next planning conversation clearer. Private understanding can remain worthwhile alongside, rather than subordinate to, the work result.

check.question: Which final conclusion fits the supplied trial?
check.correct: The colleagues demonstrated particular new contributions with support; the unfamiliar task and unsupplied experience remain separate questions.
wrong: The trial establishes permanent mastery and equitable opportunity across DHS.
The unfamiliar example proves every earlier contribution was worthless.
Private understanding counts only after a new workplace score is published.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The result is useful at its actual scope without erasing new conditions or making personal learning instrumental.
check.feedbackIncorrect: One trial cannot establish permanent mastery or agency-wide equity. A new example does not erase the earlier supported contributions. Private understanding needs no published work score. Each alternative expands a limited result or dismisses meaningful learning without evidence.

items.text: Kei prepared a usable comparison with the checked example.
Dia says the source inquiry clarified the explanation’s limit.
Preparation needed for the unfamiliar example.
Another colleague’s experience is not supplied.
Everyone permanently masters every team responsibility.
Private insight requires a public productivity score.

lessons.next: You can now describe particular contributions, understand different meanings of showing ability, combine skills and propose supported growth without fixed personal types.

scenario.context: DSD practice case: The closing note claims permanent strengths types and universal mastery from the supported trial. The next task is unfamiliar and another colleague’s account is absent.
options: Declare no value because another preparation question exists.
Infer that the absent colleague approved every arrangement.
Describe the specific new contributions and retain the changed task and missing experience as open.
responses: A new condition does not erase the actual practice result.
This recognizes the supported progress and keeps the next inquiry at its proper scope.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain a specific contribution, one next condition and a learned meaning of showing ability.

move.control: You can update a strengths discussion using evidence, interests and relevant conditions.
move.failure: A useful trial becomes a permanent type, unlimited expectation or universal claim.

jobAid.subtitle: Recognize real contributions and use them as a starting point for connection and growth.
remember: A strength description names the action, useful effect and conditions; it is not a permanent personality.
Demonstrated skill, stated interest and needed support answer different questions.
Recognize preparation as well as a public contribution without inferring cultural types.
A supported opportunity can be precise and modest without guaranteeing an employment outcome.
Actual authority and reporting duties remain; private self-understanding is legitimate without a work score.

sections.heading: Describe and understand
items: What did the person contribute in this example, and how did it help?
Which material, preparation or support made the contribution possible?
What interest has the person actually stated, rather than what have others inferred?
Use the original Rosa/Vale fiction to consider different meanings of visibility without borrowing a type to explain a colleague.

sections.heading: Connect and develop
items: Explain how the contributions connect to the same actual task and which condition each cannot answer alone.
Define a particular practice part, suitable preparation and relevant feedback through actual assignment roles.
Examine current responsibilities instead of treating praise as unlimited availability.
Keep source, approval and selection responsibilities within real authority; the consultant leads program guidance and feedback while staff do their own work.

sections.heading: Review at the right scope
items: Describe the particular example and actual accounts. A missing perspective remains unknown.
Revisit preparation when the task changes; progress does not establish permanent mastery.
Use required DHS equity analysis where the actual policy applies.

Managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. Learning makes no finding and delays no duty.
Native American- and Tribal-specific matters go to the person or area responsible within ADSA.

sources.title: Canada School of Public Service: Team Charter Guidelines
sources.note: The skills/knowledge and desired-development questions support a bounded planning example. Canadian guidance creates no Minnesota assessment requirement, assignment authority, rotation rule or review cadence.

sources.title: U.S. Surgeon General: Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being
sources.note: The original 2022 framework’s growth, preparation and relevant reciprocal-feedback guidance informs planning. No survey figure, health prediction, promotion promise or Minnesota employment mandate is inferred.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Personalized contextual meanings, wider perspective and intrinsic self-understanding inform the original Rosa/Vale encounter. No group profile or required personal disclosure is created.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Actual daily equity responsibility and formal analysis for qualifying prolonged or long-term actions scheduled for the specified leadership approval stay separate from learning or a practice proposal.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited
sources.note: Marin’s separate allegation preserves immediate manager/supervisor reporting of all protected-class allegations or incidents, agency procedures and nonretaliation. The course supplies no finding or employment decision.
